nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Product life-cycle analysis|Disposal methods
nodes.label: Disposal methods

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Product life-cycle analysis|Disposal methods_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is the current status of municipal landfills regarding the disposal of POPs in high-income countries?
nodes.answer: Many high-income countries have disposed of POPs containing municipal waste in landfills, and countries like Australia, New Zealand, and the US still do so due to limited waste destruction capacity.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Product life-cycle analysis|Disposal methods_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Are inventories developed for POPs disposed of in landfills within the framework of the Stockholm Convention?
nodes.answer: Inventories of POPs disposed of in landfills or contaminated sites are typically not quantified, with few exceptions such as large pesticide landfills.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Product life-cycle analysis|Disposal methods_qna_002
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What was the common method of disposal for chemical production wastes in industrial countries before the 1970s?
nodes.answer: Chemical production wastes, including POPs, were largely landfilled or dumped.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Product life-cycle analysis|Disposal methods_qna_003
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What happens to products containing POPs and PBTs at the end of their life?
nodes.answer: They end up in the waste stream.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Product life-cycle analysis|Disposal methods_qna_004
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What has been the traditional method of handling SPL?
nodes.answer: The traditional method of handling SPL has been landfilling, as it was the most economically feasible option.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Product life-cycle analysis|Disposal methods_qna_005
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What commonality is noted among the studies by Schmidt et al. (2004a) and Murphy and Norton (2008)?
nodes.answer: Both studies implemented end-of-life scenario analysis to compare the environmental impacts of products when they are landfilled, incinerated, or composted.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Product life-cycle analysis|Disposal methods_qna_006
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Why are products being disposed of quickly and ending up mostly landfilled or incinerated?
nodes.answer: Products are being used for shorter periods of time due to overconsumption culture and poor durability, leading to massive disposals that often end up landfilled or incinerated, particularly in countries with inadequate waste management systems and limited recycling infrastructure.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Product life-cycle analysis|Disposal methods_qna_007
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How will the inventory of identified waste management practices be used by scholars?
nodes.answer: It will serve as a starting point for scholars evaluating the sustainability of identified waste management practices.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Sustainable consumption and production|Product life-cycle analysis|Disposal methods_qna_008
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: Is it economically viable for companies to comply with waste disposal regulations?
nodes.answer: Sometimes there is a belief that alternative, often illicit methods of waste disposal may generate savings, but not properly disposing of waste can lead to additional costs in the long run.
